records.name: Kaelvar
records.summary: A northwestern continent of dry interior uplands, fertile southern coasts, and island-studded northern waters.
civilizationNotes: Dwarven mountain networks anchor the western highlands.
Elves hold hidden river-valley and southern forest enclaves.
Orc tribes roam the dry interior plains.
strategicNotes: Kaelvar's interior is a natural conflict zone between settled southern powers and mobile tribal groups.

densityNotes: Southern coasts are high-density farming and port lands.
Western plateau is low-density frontier terrain.
Northern islands are settled but sparse.
populationProfile.settlementPattern: Southern coasts cluster dense ports and estates while the interior depends on marches, mines, and caravan forts.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Southern coasts cluster dense ports and estates while the interior depends on marches, mines, and caravan forts.

records.name: Valtherion
records.summary: The largest and most fertile landmass, dominated by major rivers, forested northlands, and vast agricultural basins.
civilizationNotes: Valtherion is the primary world civilization center.
Human kingdoms line the river basins.
Ancient elven forest realms dominate northern woodlands.
Dwarves inhabit mountain chains and canyon cities.
strategicNotes: Valtherion's border kingdoms and chokepoints make it the political center of the map.

densityNotes: Major river basins support dense cities and farm belts.
populationProfile.settlementPattern: Dense basin and river corridors support the largest settlement mesh in the world.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Dense basin and river corridors support the largest settlement mesh in the world.

records.name: Serathyl
records.summary: A long maritime continent of complex coasts, forested interiors, and merchant-friendly sea lanes.
civilizationNotes: Human merchant republics line the coasts.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Ports and estuaries are dense, while wet forests and mountains remain sparser and more specialized.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Ports and estuaries are dense, while wet forests and mountains remain sparser and more specialized.

records.name: Draemor
records.summary: A fertile southern central continent defined by large river systems and powerful agricultural belts.
civilizationNotes: The central river basin supports enormous food production.
Large dwarven tunnel cities exist beneath the central hills.

densityNotes: The central basin supports enormous food production.
populationProfile.settlementPattern: The basin can sustain dense agrarian networks with strong river market towns.

generationRules.settlementPattern: The basin can sustain dense agrarian networks with strong river market towns.

records.name: Talmyra
records.summary: A wilder southeastern continent of tribal confederacies, volcanic strongholds, jungled interiors, and contested frontiers.
civilizationNotes: Many tribal confederacies dominate the wilds.
Hidden elven enclaves survive in deep jungles.
Dwarven citadels stand in ancient volcanic ranges.
strategicNotes: Talmyra's frontier wars and spice trade shape southern sea politics.

densityNotes: Interior jungle and mountain zones are very low-density.
populationProfile.settlementPattern: Valleys and controlled coasts hold most population while harsher coasts and uplands stay specialized.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Valleys and controlled coasts hold most population while harsher coasts and uplands stay specialized.

records.name: The Auric Marches
records.summary: Golden plains, dry marches, and mineral-bearing uplands across western Kaelvar.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Sparse mining towns and caravan forts occupy water-secured breaks in the plateau.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Sparse mining towns and caravan forts occupy water-secured breaks in the plateau.

records.name: Verdant Thalos
records.summary: The lush southern peninsula of Kaelvar, rich in agriculture, ports, and managed forests.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Cities and estate belts favor the coast and vineyard corridors, with secondary towns on the farm interior.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Cities and estate belts favor the coast and vineyard corridors, with secondary towns on the farm interior.

records.name: The Shattercap Isles
records.summary: A broken northern island fringe that screens Kaelvar from the open northern sea.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Harbors and beacon cliffs dominate the small island settlement pattern.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Harbors and beacon cliffs dominate the small island settlement pattern.

records.name: The Crownlands
records.summary: Northern forests and highlands holding the oldest noble forests and elevated frontiers of Valtherion.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Forest valleys and winter strongholds support moderate settlement with protected gates and bastions.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Forest valleys and winter strongholds support moderate settlement with protected gates and bastions.

records.name: The Embersteppe
records.summary: A drier central plateau and steppe corridor between richer Valtherion basins.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Pastoral corridors and guarded wells define the viable settlement pattern.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Pastoral corridors and guarded wells define the viable settlement pattern.

records.name: The Sapphire Rivers
records.summary: The eastern river basin of Valtherion, crowded with navigable waters, cities, and farmland.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: River cities, floodplain markets, and crossing towns create the densest inland network.

generationRules.settlementPattern: River cities, floodplain markets, and crossing towns create the densest inland network.

records.name: The Jade Expanse
records.summary: A broad southern agricultural expanse where fertile lowlands feed the greater Valtherion system.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Broad agrarian settlement with horse-breeding and market corridors rather than deep forest clustering.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Broad agrarian settlement with horse-breeding and market corridors rather than deep forest clustering.

records.name: The Windward Spine
records.summary: The mountain backbone of Serathyl, shaping weather, travel, and northern settlement limits.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Pass holds, quarry towns, and alpine redoubts anchor a harsh but valuable mountain corridor.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Pass holds, quarry towns, and alpine redoubts anchor a harsh but valuable mountain corridor.

records.name: The Green Reach
records.summary: The central forested heartland of Serathyl where timber, dyes, and elven domains overlap.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Forested clearings, timber crossings, and herb-processing villages dominate the sparse network.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Forested clearings, timber crossings, and herb-processing villages dominate the sparse network.

records.name: The Sailor's Verge
records.summary: An island-rich southern maritime rim of harbors, fleets, and sea-linked republics.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Dense maritime settlement follows estuaries, ports, and rope or mast towns.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Dense maritime settlement follows estuaries, ports, and rope or mast towns.

records.name: The Heart Basin
records.summary: The core river hub and granary basin of Draemor.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: The primary southern breadbasket supports dense market towns and multiple large cities.

generationRules.settlementPattern: The primary southern breadbasket supports dense market towns and multiple large cities.

records.name: The Emerald Mantle
records.summary: The lowland belt surrounding Draemor's basin, rich in pasture, villages, and market roads.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Mixed pasture, orchard, and forest lanes support moderate-high inland settlement.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Mixed pasture, orchard, and forest lanes support moderate-high inland settlement.

records.name: The Stormcap Coast
records.summary: The rough southern shores of Draemor where storms, fisheries, and hard ports dominate.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Storm harbors and defended coast villages cluster where anchorages are reliable enough.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Storm harbors and defended coast villages cluster where anchorages are reliable enough.

records.name: The Thorn Peninsula
records.summary: The narrow southern extension of Talmyra, broken by peninsulas, cliffs, and exposed coasts.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Peninsula trade favors spice ports, fortified routes, and estate belts rather than broad urban build-out.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Peninsula trade favors spice ports, fortified routes, and estate belts rather than broad urban build-out.

records.name: The Silver Valleys
records.summary: The more habitable interior valleys of Talmyra where rivers allow denser settlement and contested agriculture.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Valley cities and ford towns are viable, while uplands favor camps, mines, and forts.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Valley cities and ford towns are viable, while uplands favor camps, mines, and forts.

records.name: The Watcher Coast
records.summary: An eastern coast of cliffs, islands, and hard maritime approaches along Talmyra's edge.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Defense, quarrying, and hard-port control matter more than agrarian settlement here.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Defense, quarrying, and hard-port control matter more than agrarian settlement here.

records.name: The Myridian Chain
records.summary: A busy archipelago between Kaelvar and Valtherion made up of pirate states, trade ports, and naval staging points.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Harbor chains and relay islands dominate settlement while interior ridges remain sparse.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Harbor chains and relay islands dominate settlement while interior ridges remain sparse.

records.name: The Lantern Isles
records.summary: Small central-ocean islands used as trade outposts, hidden anchorages, and pirate refuges.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Harbors and sheltered lagoons sustain the islands more than inland acreage does.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Harbors and sheltered lagoons sustain the islands more than inland acreage does.

records.name: The Serpent's Wake
records.summary: A storm-lashed southern island arc infamous for pirate tribes, wrecking seas, and undersea kingdoms.

notableGroups: Merfolk kingdoms beneath the surrounding waters

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Settlement survives through convoy support, salvage, and hard coastal adaptation rather than agrarian depth.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Settlement survives through convoy support, salvage, and hard coastal adaptation rather than agrarian depth.

records.name: The Dawnreach Isles
records.summary: Sparse eastern islands far from the main continental centers, valuable mainly as waypoints and remote outposts.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Tiny cold-harbor networks persist through fisheries, fur, and maritime relay work.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Tiny cold-harbor networks persist through fisheries, fur, and maritime relay work.

records.name: Starfall Isle
records.summary: The main customs island of the Myridian Chain, where relay harbors, bonded warehouses, and ferry slips crowd around the safest deepwater port in the northern archipelago.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Deepwater harbors, bonded quays, and short-haul ferry villages ring the defensible coves of the island.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Deepwater harbors, bonded quays, and short-haul ferry villages ring the defensible coves of the island.

records.name: The Pearlwake Keys
records.summary: A ring of low coral keys and shoal villages where pearl divers, salt fishers, and reef pilots work the shelves between safer Myridian anchorages.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Harbor towns and curing villages cling to the shoals while divers and pilots work the wider shelf.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Harbor towns and curing villages cling to the shoals while divers and pilots work the wider shelf.

records.name: Zenith Isle
records.summary: The highest and most exposed watch-island in the outer ring, where beacon forts, warning towers, and patrol crews guard the northern lanes into the Myridian Chain.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Small garrisons and signal keeps hold the only reliable landings on the exposed edge islands.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Small garrisons and signal keeps hold the only reliable landings on the exposed edge islands.

records.name: The Lantern Crown
records.summary: The safest surface island cluster in the Lantern Isles, where broker harbors, reef pilots, and opportunistic free ports sit behind bright reefs and seasonal gardens.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Broker harbors and market wards pack the inner coves while gardens and reef farms spread across the brighter slopes.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Broker harbors and market wards pack the inner coves while gardens and reef farms spread across the brighter slopes.

records.name: Glasswake Quay
records.summary: A quieter quay-island of shrine estates, shell kilns, and traveler refuges where herb gardens and lookout posts make the mid-ocean routes barely livable.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Monasteries, lookout outposts, and herb plots occupy the few sheltered rises above the reef line.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Monasteries, lookout outposts, and herb plots occupy the few sheltered rises above the reef line.

records.name: Deepglow Reef
records.summary: A luminous reef shelf and sea-cave complex beneath the islands, home to hidden merfolk craft halls, pearl beds, and submerged exchange routes.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Merfolk enclaves and hidden exchange chambers cluster through the reef shelf rather than across the exposed surface.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Merfolk enclaves and hidden exchange chambers cluster through the reef shelf rather than across the exposed surface.

records.name: Stormfang Isle
records.summary: One of the few larger islands in the Wake with a harbor deep enough for repair yards, convoy musters, and rough law to coexist beneath the storms.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Repair coves, salvage yards, and hard fishing wards hold the only denser settlement around the island's safer anchorages.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Repair coves, salvage yards, and hard fishing wards hold the only denser settlement around the island's safer anchorages.

records.name: The Blackreef Keys
records.summary: A broken spread of black-stone reefs and pirate anchorages where smuggling, raiding, and storm salvage remain the surest economy.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Tiny pirate holds and salvage camps occupy hidden channels between reef-torn islets.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Tiny pirate holds and salvage camps occupy hidden channels between reef-torn islets.

records.name: Stormhook Reach
records.summary: The outer watch islands of the Wake, marked by signal heights, escort musters, and settlements small enough to live or vanish by convoy season.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Signal crews, escorts, and seasonal camps occupy the only viable pockets between weather breaks.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Signal crews, escorts, and seasonal camps occupy the only viable pockets between weather breaks.

records.name: Aurora Reach
records.summary: The most viable harbor belt in Dawnreach, where cold-water anchorages, cod fleets, and ice pilots keep a thin eastward trade alive.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Harbor hamlets and whaling quays survive where cliffs and current give rare shelter from the eastern sea.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Harbor hamlets and whaling quays survive where cliffs and current give rare shelter from the eastern sea.

records.name: The Nacre Shelf
records.summary: A rare sheltered shelf beneath Dawnreach where nacre caverns, pearl beds, and merfolk craft halls survive below the worst of the weather.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Merfolk neighborhoods and craft halls cluster along the shelf rather than on the storm-struck surface.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Merfolk neighborhoods and craft halls cluster along the shelf rather than on the storm-struck surface.

records.name: Whalebone Edge
records.summary: An exposed rim of lookout islands and processing camps where whales, seals, and storms decide whether a season pays or kills.

populationProfile.settlementPattern: Lookout camps and whale-processing stations endure only on the hardest coasts and only for as long as the season allows.

generationRules.settlementPattern: Lookout camps and whale-processing stations endure only on the hardest coasts and only for as long as the season allows.

records.name: The Azure Vast
records.summary: The central ocean binding the world map together through trade, piracy, and long-haul navigation.
strategicNotes: The Azure Vast is the main connective sea between all five continents.

records.name: The Gilded Sea
records.summary: A prosperous western sea adjacent to Valtherion and the northern island routes.
strategicNotes: This sea ties Valtherion to the Myridian routes and northwest exchanges.

records.name: The Tempest Expanse
records.summary: The storm-heavy southern ocean where climate and distance make navigation costly and dangerous.
strategicNotes: The Tempest Expanse amplifies the risks around southern islands and long ocean routes.

records.name: The Shattered Gulf
records.summary: A broken gulf between Serathyl and Draemor filled with sea lanes, island approaches, and contested shipping.
strategicNotes: The gulf is a natural maritime fault line between western merchants and southern grain routes.
